summary: "Space Cadets" is an interactive mission trainer project hosted on Netlify that integrates real-world NASA space data to quiz and track users on solar flares. By pulling live information—such as an X5.1 monster flare from November 2025—directly from the NASA Donkey Database, the game educates players on flare classifications ranging progressively through A, B, C, M, and X classes, where each category is ten times more powerful than the preceding one.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: Commander Certification

What it does: A browser game where kids command a Mars base and answer 9 random science questions, drawn from a bank of 50, against a 5-minute clock. The questions cover power trade-offs, radiation safety, life support and space science. Prof. Orbit explains every answer. Correct answers play a dhol beat and raise the base’s meters; wrong ones play a sad trombone. Each mission includes one question built from real solar flares pulled live from NASA’s DONKI API. It ends with a learning report showing the score, rank and accuracy per skill, plus a scoreboard.

Benefits & impact: Makes space science hands-on and fun. Kids learn why surviving on Mars or the Moon is hard, and how to make smart trade-offs like real mission planners. It’s free, needs no install, works on any device, and gives teachers a quick view of what each child understands.

Tools:

  • Game: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with SVG and Canvas for graphics and the Web Audio API for all sound.
  • NASA data: the DONKI solar-flare API via api.nasa.gov.
  • Videos: Python with Skia and FFmpeg, the open-source Kokoro text-to-speech voice, and Playwright for game screen captures.
  • AI: built with help from Claude (AI assistant). Runs on standard laptops.

Creativity: An original mascot (Prof. Orbit), a dhol celebration for correct answers, base meters that react to what you know, and quiz questions generated from the real Sun’s current activity.

Factors considered: Age-appropriate language, scientific accuracy, honest labels for live vs. archived data, an offline fallback, accessibility (keyboard, touch, captions, mute), no personal data collected, and replayability.
